advice: Abstain from proposing another scratch stride. The supplied evidence gives a 128-byte cache line and 128 KiB P-core L1D, but no cache-set indexing or associativity to justify a new padding choice. The earlier 320-byte proposal has no supplied measurement, and the 272-byte layout was measured and rejected. Neither supports selecting another stride. Keep the current 256-byte stride unless a distinct layout is selected for swarm review.
risks: No scratch cache-conflict benefit is established. Padding increases allocation and packing costs and can introduce bounds or correctness errors. Any future selected variant needs exact allocation, consumer offsets, and rewinds checked, then full-call measurement including allocation and packing, with ten validation reports and ten fresh alternating paired controls under the unchanged gates. The joint TRANS_B results do not test or establish effects from scratch layout.
